what: American Healthcare REIT owns senior housing, skilled nursing facilities and medical office buildings, and unusually it operates much of the senior housing itself rather than only collecting rent.
customers: Older Americans living in its communities, and the physician practices leasing its medical offices.
money: medical offices and leased nursing facilities
moat: Operating the communities rather than leasing them means capturing the full upside when occupancy and rates rise, which is what has been happening as the over-80 population grows.
risks: Operating senior housing means carrying staffing costs directly, and wages have risen sharply
118 times earnings, because operating costs leave little accounting profit
Free cash flow was heavily negative as the company bought out partners and expanded
opportunities: Revenue grew from $1.1B to $2.3B in four years as occupancy recovered
Analysts see about 15% upside, with 16 covering the stock
Almost no new senior housing is being built while the over-80 population grows quickly
watch: Same-store occupancy and margin in the operating senior housing portfolio.
